text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Twelve members of the international environment organisation Greenpeace blocked the office of the Maltese prime minister on Monday by chaining themselves across the entrance. They insist the government should urgently tackle the island's waste disposal problems. Environment Minister George Vella said the protest was unfair because the government, in office for only 10 months, was already urgently tackling the problem and examining new waste disposal technology.

- Fewer refugees, but problems get worse. The Emigrants' Commission, which is the Malta representative of the United Nations High Commission for Refugees, said the number of refugees in Malta had been halved to 443, but problems were getting more complicated as resettlement in other countries became more difficult.
- Police tell campers to leave site being occupied illegally.
- New American Charge d'Affaires takes over with no word yet on the appointment of a new ambassador. The last ambassador, Joseph Paolino, left last year for an unsuccessful run for the U.S. congress.
- Boy in danger of dying after car crash.
